title: Table 43. I/O current injection susceptibility
text_helper: Table 43. I/O current injection susceptibility — section 6.3.13 I/O current injection characteristics. Symbol, Description, Functional susceptibility / Negative injection, Functional susceptibility / Positive injection, Unit.

rows: Injected current on BOOT0 and PF1 pins
Injected current on PA9, PB3, PB13, PF11 pins with induced leakage current on adjacent pins less than 50 µA
Injected current on PA11 and PA12 pins with induced leakage current on adjacent pins less than -1 mA
Injected current on all other FT and FTf pins
Injected current on PB0 and PB1 pins
Injected current on all other TTa, TC and RST pins
notes: 1. Data based on design simulation only. Not tested in production.
2. The leakage could be higher than the maximum value, if negative current is injected on adjacent pins. Refer to Table 43: I/O current injection susceptibility.
3. To sustain a voltage higher than V + 0.3 V, the internal pull-up/pull-down resistors must be disabled. DDIOx
4. Pull-up and pull-down resistors are designed with a true resistance in series with a switchable PMOS/NMOS. This PMOS/NMOS contribution to the series resistance is minimal (~10% order).
